methodological_rigor.justification: A single-site diagnostic pilot evaluating a custom intraoral MLX90614 infrared sensor against histopathology on only 10 OSCC patients and 10 healthy controls. The selected OSCC cases are biopsy-confirmed, but eight of 18 initially evaluated patients were excluded (recurrent lesions, non-OSCC pathology, prior surgery), and the control group is recruited separately and is not matched by age or sex. Sample size calculation claims only 8 per group based on a 0.10 degree C difference which is implausibly small given the reported 0.3 degree C sensor accuracy. The near-perfect AUC, sensitivity = 1.0 and specificity = 1.0 from 20 individuals is highly suggestive of overfitting and unrepresentative case selection (only tongue and lip SCC, excluding smokers and all premalignant lesions). The reported 43 +/- 26 year mean age with a 26-year SD is implausibly wide and suggests age-related and anatomic confounding.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a registered clinical trial (IRCT20181130041806N1), but by design it is a diagnostic accuracy pilot on 20 highly selected participants without blinding and without a spectrum of benign/premalignant controls, mapping to Oxford LoE 4. Even if replicated, a probe that detects a difference in temperature at visible tongue/lip OSCC lesions that are already clinically suspicious offers limited incremental value over the clinical exam plus biopsy pathway that triggers the test; translational relevance is therefore preliminary and contingent on future spectrum studies.

reporting_quality.justification: STARD is the appropriate standard for diagnostic accuracy reporting but is not referenced and no checklist is provided. A flow diagram (Figure 1) is described. Key STARD items are missing: no description of blinding of index-test and reference-standard interpretation, no reporting of indeterminate results, no confidence intervals for sensitivity/specificity, no information on consecutive/random recruitment, and an unexplained exclusion of four cases because pathology was 'not OSCC' undermines spectrum assessment. No data or code availability is mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors introduce a custom-designed, portable, wireless, ergonomic intraoral IR-sensor device (MLX90614) aimed at oral-cavity-specific temperature sensing, which is a modest engineering advance over Chakraborty and colleagues' facial thermography approaches (refs 10, 11, 29). The underlying principle (tumour metabolism produces higher local temperatures) and its use in skin and breast cancer thermography are well established. Novelty is primarily in device design and intraoral application rather than in biological concept.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript follows a standard IMRAD structure and is readable. Device description and procedures are reasonably detailed. However, there are inconsistencies: participant counts fluctuate between sections (28 initially vs 18 patients vs 10 included), the mean age of 43 +/- 26 years is presented without separate case/control breakdowns, and the Discussion drifts into repetitive restatement of prior thermography literature. Figures and tables are described only by captions in the provided text.

key_strengths: Registered clinical trial (IRCT20181130041806N1) with ethics approval and histopathology as reference standard
Engineering contribution of a portable, wireless intraoral IR probe (MLX90614, 0.02 degree C resolution) with ergonomic and ISO 13485 design considerations
Pre-measurement standardization (30 min fasting, 20 min acclimatization at 24 degree C) supports measurement reliability
key_concerns: Extremely small sample (10 cases, 10 controls) with reported sensitivity and specificity of 1.0, strongly suggestive of overfitting and selection bias
Spectrum bias: premalignant lesions, benign inflammatory conditions, and non-tongue/lip OSCC are all excluded, so the index test has not been challenged against realistic differential diagnoses
Controls are not matched to cases and participant counts fluctuate between sections (28 vs 18 vs 10)
No STARD checklist, no blinding description, no confidence intervals for diagnostic metrics, and no data/code availability
The 0.10 degree C sample size assumption is inconsistent with the device's 0.3 degree C accuracy specification
Claimed cutoffs (>0.97 degree C difference; >38.42 degree C absolute) are derived and tested on the same 20 participants without internal cross-validation or external cohort
chief_reviewer.rationale: A small pilot diagnostic study whose perfect accuracy metrics are not credible given the sample size and severe spectrum bias; best fit is Tier 4 with major revisions including a larger, prospectively recruited cohort with premalignant and benign controls, STARD-compliant reporting, and blinded interpretation.
